pr.title: Report review label changes to the fixer and reload the panel on events
pr.head: 7b55da5a87f3bfe1f9078bfed1bf3791a2ea9b12

summary: Projector's watch daemon is one process per machine that polls the pull requests agent sessions subscribe to, and appends one-line events to each session's events file. A session that pushed a pull request owns its fix role and hears about review work on it, such as an open finding thread. Projector's reviews mark their outcome with two labels: reviewing while a review runs, and clean once a review signs the current head off.

Before this change, the daemon fetched the labels only so Projector's panel in Claude Code could draw them. No event reported a change to them, so the fixing session never heard that a review had started or signed its head off. This change adds a LABEL event for the fix owner, such as LABEL acme/app#12 +clean head=9f3c2a1b: … tell the user it is clean. It also makes the panel reload as soon as it takes a batch of events, so an open drawer shows threads that match the events rather than ones up to 30 seconds old.

• Edge-triggered, not level-triggered. The daemon's other fix events repeat while their work stands. A LABEL line fires once per change, because it reports news rather than work.
  • A silent first look. The first time an owner sees a pull request, and the first time after the role moves to a new owner, the daemon records the labels and sends nothing. An upgrade, or a subscription to a pull request that is already clean, sends no burst of lines.
  • Fixers only. A session that owns the review role hears nothing, because its own reviews set the labels.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding: the in-progress watch-daemon plan at docs/projects/watch-daemon/readme.md still lists no LABEL event in its § 2.7 event table. Its § 9.3 still says the drawer's threads stay on the 30-second poll.
  • Two suggestions: say in docs/plugins.md that the event reload is a whole poll, and give the route_labels docstring the host-neutral reason for the silent first look.
  • The full Python suite, claude plugin test ., both plugin validations, hooks/typecheck.sh, project check, and git diff --check pass at this head.

groups.title: The daemon reports label changes
groups.kicker: A LABEL event for the fix owner, and the record it compares against
intro: Each pass, route_fix works out what the session that owns a pull request's fix role should hear. It now ends by calling route_labels, which compares the pull request's clean and reviewing labels with the ones the session last saw and sends a LABEL line for each one added or removed.

The labels the session last saw live in a new labels section of the session's state.json, keyed like the fix record. Pass.save drops a session's entries for every role it no longer owns, and now applies that to labels too. So a closed pull request, or a role handed to another session, leaves no record behind, and the next owner starts with a silent first look.

checks.text: A label edit changes the ETag of the pull request's REST resource, so refresh queries the pull request again on the next pass rather than waiting for the full query. Traced through Pass.refresh.

files.note: Adds LABEL_CHANGES, the text each change sends, route_labels, and the labels state section.

checks.text: Labels are lowercased before they are compared, as review.label_names does, because GitHub treats label names without regard to case.

The new record is written before the comparison returns, so the next pass compares against this pass's labels and a renotify interval does not repeat a line. The 900-second step in the first new test checks it.
The filter that drops a non-owned role's record now covers labels. The pull request's testing section says the closed-pull-request and handover tests fail without it.

files.note: Five tests: the change sequence, a non-review label, a review owner, a close, and a handover.

groups.title: The panel reloads when it takes events
groups.kicker: One refresh call in the mod's event delivery
intro: Projector's mod for Claude Code delivers the daemon's events. On each 5-second tick it takes the lines from the session's events file and submits them as one prompt. While the panel is shown, it also draws each pull request from the daemon's cache on each tick, but asks GitHub for the open drawer's threads only every 30 seconds.

deliverEvents now calls refresh as soon as it takes a batch. The daemon writes a pull request's cache during its pass and appends the events only at the end of the pass, so the reload draws what the events report. refresh runs a whole poll by default, which reads the drawer's threads, panel.background, and any pull request an earlier watcher tracks.

checks.text: refresh does nothing while the panel is hidden, and its inFlight guard queues a request that arrives during a tick's own refresh, so the two never run at once.

files.note: Calls refresh once a batch of events is taken, before it is submitted.

checks.text: The pull request's testing section says the new panel test fails without this call. Between polls a tick asks GitHub for no threads, so the count would stay at one.

files.note: Opens a drawer, writes a cache update and a LABEL event between polls, and expects a second thread query on the next tick.

groups.title: Documentation and the fix-pr skill
groups.kicker: What the new event means, and what a fixing session does with it
intro: docs/cli.md adds the event to the daemon's event table and explains the silent first look. skills/fix-pr/SKILL.md tells a fixing session that a LABEL line is not work: on +clean it tells the user, and it does nothing for the other changes. docs/plugins.md says the open drawer also reads its threads when the panel takes events.

files.note: A LABEL row in the event table, and a paragraph on when the daemon records labels.

checks.text: The watch-daemon plan, at status: in-progress, lists the daemon's events in its § 2.7 table and has no LABEL row. Its § 9.3 still says the drawer's threads, panel.background, and the earlier watcher's query stay on the 30-second poll. The repository asks a change to update the plan whose decisions it settles, and every earlier change to watch.py updated this one.
